P1.interpretation: COLLAPSED: Real ΔD (5.7) is LESS than null median (7.9). The D-variation observed across scales is consistent with what pure single-S2 produces under the same fitting procedure. The 3-scale fitting pipeline itself introduces spurious D-variation. P1 does NOT support T7.

P2.direction: dust LESS favored at fine scale (opposite of T7 prediction)
P2.interpretation: NOT SUPPORTED: The paired Wilcoxon test shows multi-component fits are NOT more favored at finer resolution. In fact, the direction is opposite — dust is LESS favored at fine scale. T7 prediction P2 is not confirmed.

P3.interpretation: SUPPORTED: Within-system (between-scale) variance is 3.1x the between-system variance. This means D varies more across probe scales within the same system than it varies across different systems. This is consistent with T7 (D is scale-dependent, not system-invariant). CAVEAT: part of this within-system variance may be fitting artifact (see P1 null result).

P4.interpretation: Meta-S2 (Weibull law for D distribution) is FALSIFIED. This supports dropping Meta-S2 as a foundational claim, but does NOT independently confirm T7. The D distribution being non-Weibull is consistent with many hypotheses, not uniquely T7.

honest_summary: T7 INTERFERENCE HYPOTHESIS — PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. The decisive null-model control test (P1) COLLAPSED: real D-variation across scales (median ΔD=5.7) is LESS than what synthetic single-S2 data produces under the identical fitting procedure (null median ΔD=7.9, Mann-Whitney p=0.76). The observed scale-dependence of D is consistent with a fitting artifact, not evidence of interference. P2 (multi-component at fine scale) is NOT supported — paired Wilcoxon p=0.97, direction opposite to T7 prediction. P3 (hierarchical variance) is nominally supported (within/between=3.1), but this may also reflect the fitting artifact identified in P1. P4 (Meta-S2 falsified) removes an alternative but does not confirm T7. CONCLUSION: The interference hypothesis remains theoretically motivated by the 10D→4D compression axioms, but the current registry does NOT provide empirical support beyond what single-S2 plus fitting effects would produce. Distinguishing genuine interference from fitting artifacts requires a more refined experimental design.
critical_finding: The 3-scale fitting procedure itself introduces substantial D-variation even on pure single-S2 data. This means the original P1 result (100% of datasets showing D variation) was measuring the fitting procedures sensitivity to sub-range selection, not genuine scale-dependent interference. This is exactly the control test that was needed.
